title: Complete the first How We Know evidence experience
objective: Supersede EM-0020 with authority to compile the first accepted How We Know dossier across human and machine interfaces while correcting every compiled current-state document to distinguish the bounded application-level dossier graph from the self-describing repository corpus and the still-unimplemented normative replay architecture.
required_evaluation: lineage-count derivation and shared-ancestor adversarial tests
HTML, Markdown, JSON, API, MCP, and CLI parity tests
compiled README and launch-document current-state audit
external route and content-type read-back after accepted deployment
acceptance: the homepage leads with one accepted finding about the world rather than a directory of project internals
a reader can reveal the exact accepted edition and span behind every material dossier sentence
raw mention count and independent-lineage count are visibly distinguished and deterministically reproduced
encyclopedia and skeptical views share the accepted source objects while producing a material, explained policy-relative difference
contradictions, qualifiers, unknown dependence, and unresolved defeaters remain visible
the existing self-describing project corpus remains available through Explore and documentation routes

README and launch-facing documentation accurately distinguish the implemented application-level dossier projection from the target normative replay architecture and from externally unverified deployment
the featured selection is an explicit accepted compiler input rather than detached hand-authored marketing
all public interfaces expose the same dossier, catalog, frontier, policies, compiler, accepted commit, and content digest
make check passes without changing accepted source state
the accepted Pages deployment passes route, canonical URL, keyboard, mobile, content-type, and manifest read-back
limitations: This task does not claim that one dossier validates the full Epistemedia thesis, that the application-level dossier model is the normative event graph, or that the promoted policies are universally correct.
Correct current-state documentation does not prove a hosted deployment; live status still requires provider and route read-back.
Hosted API/MCP activation, automated capture, scaled seeding, and federation remain separate tasks.
Human-comprehension claims require real-reader evidence rather than synthetic review.
